text: Question: The nurse is preparing to teach an in-service for nursing staff about post operative care for the client following abdominal surgery. Which content should the nurse speak about in the in-service? Select all that apply.
A. “Therapeutic touch is an effective way to decrease postoperative abdominal pain.”
B. “Total body relaxation is an effective adjunct for postoperative pain management.”
C. “The nursing process is linear throughout the postoperative care of clients who have had abdominal surgery.”

D. “The nurse’s priority is to check on the client who had abdominal surgery and returned to the unit just now and then check on the client who is requesting pain medication and returned from abdominal surgery 12 hours ago.”

Correct answers: A. “Therapeutic touch is an effective way to decrease postoperative abdominal pain.”; B. “Total body relaxation is an effective adjunct for postoperative pain management.”; D. “The nurse’s priority is to check on the client who had abdominal surgery and returned to the unit just now and then check on the client who is requesting pain medication and returned from abdominal surgery 12 hours ago.”
notes: • Therapeutic touch and total body relaxation are accepted non-drug adjuncts for post-operative pain.
• The newly returned post-operative client is seen first (airway, vital signs, bleeding) before the client at 12 hours who wants pain medication.
Not correct: The nursing process is not linear; it is continuous and cyclical, so assessment and evaluation keep repeating.
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.) The therapeutic touch option is the least certain part of this key.

text: Question: The nurse is preparing to teach an in-service for nursing staff and students about total parenteral nutrition. Which information should the nurse include in the in-service? Select all that apply.
A. “Clients with paralytic ileus or severe diarrhea are candidates for parenteral nutrition.”
B. “Total parenteral nutrition is delivered for the client through a gastrostomy or nasogastric tube.”
C. “Protein, electrolyte, and glucose nutritional imbalances may be supplemented with total parenteral nutrition.”
D. “Clients who need long-term nutritional supplementation will receive total parenteral nutrition via IV solutions comprised of 5% dextrose.”

Correct answers: A. “Clients with paralytic ileus or severe diarrhea are candidates for parenteral nutrition.”; C. “Protein, electrolyte, and glucose nutritional imbalances may be supplemented with total parenteral nutrition.”
notes: Correct: TPN is for clients who cannot use the GI tract (for example paralytic ileus or severe diarrhea) and can supplement protein, electrolytes and glucose.
• Tube feeding through a gastrostomy or nasogastric tube is enteral nutrition; TPN is given by IV.
• Long-term TPN is given through a central line in concentrated dextrose solutions; 5% dextrose supplies too few calories.
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)
